questions.prompt: The term "over-driving" your headlights at night means:
questions.explanation: You over-drive your headlights when you travel so fast that your stopping distance is longer than the distance your headlights light up. Slow down so you can stop within the lit area. Key words: "over-driving".

choices.text: The driver cannot see clearly for 1000 metres
The low beam headlights are not set properly
The driver is travelling at a speed which would not permit them to see an object in time to stop
The driver has had the headlights on for too long

questions.prompt: If the vehicle's right tires travel off the paved portion of the roadway:
questions.explanation: Don't brake hard or turn the wheel sharply; either can cause a skid or send you across the road. Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and steer gently back onto the pavement once you have slowed down.

choices.text: Apply the brakes firmly and counter-steer to return to the paved portion of the roadway
Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the gas pedal, and then gradually return to the paved portion of the roadway
Accelerate slightly, then turn the steering wheel sharply to return to the paved portion of the roadway
Move the vehicle completely off the paved portion, then steer back onto the paved portion of the roadway

questions.prompt: According to the Basic License Driver's Handbook, most skids are the result of:
questions.explanation: Most skids happen because the driver goes too fast for the conditions, or brakes, accelerates or steers too sharply. Adjusting your driving to the conditions prevents them.

questions.prompt: In reduced visibility due to fog, smoke or snow, use the:
questions.explanation: High beams reflect off fog, smoke and snow, creating glare that makes it harder to see. Low beams light the road without that glare. Key words: "fog, smoke or snow".

questions.prompt: In a vehicle that does not have anti-lock brakes, threshold braking refers to:
questions.explanation: Threshold braking means pressing the brake firmly up to the point just before the wheels lock, and easing off slightly if they do lock. It stops you quickly while you can still steer. Key words: "threshold braking".

choices.text: Applying an even braking force to the point just before the wheels lock, and easing off slightly if the wheels lock
Pumping the brake pedal repeatedly until the vehicle comes to a stop
Releasing pressure on the brake pedal, then reapplying pressure until the wheels lock
Applying enough force to the brake pedal to lock the wheels and keep them locked

questions.prompt: A driver must report a collision to the police when anyone is injured or killed, or when the combined damage to all vehicles and property is at least:
questions.explanation: Report a collision to police if anyone is injured or killed, or if the combined damage to all vehicles and property is $5,000 or more. The limit was raised from $2,000 on January 1, 2024. Key words: "all vehicles and property".

questions.prompt: At what minimum distance must headlights be dimmed at night when approaching another vehicle from behind?
questions.explanation: Switch to low beams within 150 metres of a vehicle you are following, and within 300 metres of an oncoming vehicle. Key words: "dimmed", "from behind".

questions.prompt: In the Basic License Driver's Handbook, "night time" is defined as the period of time:
questions.explanation: Under Alberta's rules of the road, night time runs from one hour after sunset to one hour before the next sunrise. Headlights must be on during this time. Key words: "nighttime".

choices.text: Beginning 1 hour before sunset and ending 1 hour after the following sunrise
Beginning at sunset and ending at the following sunrise
Beginning 1 hour after sunset and ending 1 hour before the following sunrise

questions.prompt: When a driver's vehicle is approached by an emergency vehicle sounding a siren, from any direction on a two-way road, the driver must:
questions.explanation: An emergency vehicle with its siren on has the right-of-way. Pull over as close as possible to the right curb or edge of the road, stop, and stay stopped until it has passed. Don't stop in an intersection.

choices.text: Continue at a reduced speed and allow sufficient space for the emergency vehicle to pass
Turn on their four-way hazard lights
Stop only when the emergency vehicle has difficulty in passing
Drive as close as possible to the right curb or edge of the road and stop

questions.prompt: When following an emergency vehicle with its lights or siren activated, stay back a minimum distance of:
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive within 150 metres of an emergency vehicle that has its siren or flashing lights on. Key words: "emergency vehicle", "stay back a minimum distance".

questions.prompt: Your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS). How should you brake in an emergency?
questions.explanation: With ABS, apply steady, firm pressure to the brake pedal. Don't pump or release it, and steer where you want to go. (Driver's Guide p. 78)

choices.text: Press until the wheels lock, then release
Apply steady, firm pressure and don't pump the pedal

questions.prompt: During hard braking in a vehicle with ABS, you feel the brake pedal vibrate. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: ABS cycles the brakes on each wheel, which you feel as a vibration through the pedal. This is normal. Keep steady pressure on the pedal. (Driver's Guide p. 78)

choices.text: The brakes are failing; release the pedal
The ABS is working normally; keep steady pressure
You should pump the brake pedal instead

questions.prompt: Your vehicle begins to skid. What should you do with the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: It is very important to keep your foot off the brake if you start to skid. Look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. (Driver's Guide p. 79)

choices.text: Press it as hard as possible
Keep your foot off the brake

questions.prompt: Your wheels spin because you accelerated too quickly (a power skid). What should you do?
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas so the wheels stop spinning, make any needed steering corrections without over-correcting, then accelerate gently. (Driver's Guide p. 79)

choices.text: Take your foot off the gas and steer where you want to go

questions.prompt: You are going too fast in a turn and the vehicle slides sideways (a cornering skid). What should you do?
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas, don't use the brakes, and look and steer where you want the front of the vehicle to go. (Driver's Guide p. 79)

choices.text: Take your foot off the gas, don't brake, and steer where you want to go
Steer sharply in the opposite direction

questions.prompt: Your vehicle breaks down. Where should you avoid stopping?
questions.explanation: Don't stop on a bridge or in a tunnel. This can be very dangerous. Move to a safe location if possible. (Driver's Guide p. 80)

choices.text: On the shoulder of a highway
On a bridge or in a tunnel

questions.prompt: When your vehicle breaks down on a highway, how far apart should you place reflective triangles behind it?
questions.explanation: Place reflective triangles to the rear of your vehicle, about 10 to 20 metres apart. (Driver's Guide p. 80)

choices.text: Directly behind the vehicle, touching the bumper

questions.prompt: Your vehicle has broken down in a dangerous spot. Where should you and your passengers wait for help?
questions.explanation: Have everyone leave the vehicle and wait at a safe location away from the vehicle and to the rear of it. (Driver's Guide p. 80)

choices.text: Inside the vehicle with seat belts on
On the road beside the vehicle to flag down help
Away from the vehicle, to the rear of it

questions.prompt: A front tire goes flat while you are driving. What should you do first?
questions.explanation: Resist the urge to brake immediately. Take your foot off the gas, hold the wheel firmly, and keep the vehicle straight. Then brake gently and pull over. (Driver's Guide p. 81)

choices.text: Take your foot off the gas and hold the steering wheel firmly

questions.prompt: Your power steering fails while driving. What happens?
questions.explanation: You can still steer the vehicle, but you'll need extra effort to turn the steering wheel. (Driver's Guide p. 81)

choices.text: You can no longer steer at all
You can still steer, but it takes more effort

questions.prompt: Both of your headlights fail at night. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard lights and try switching the headlights off and on. If they don't come back, slow down and pull over somewhere safe. (Driver's Guide p. 81)

choices.text: Keep driving with your high beams
Drive slowly to the nearest service station
Turn on your hazard lights, try the headlight switch, then pull over safely

questions.prompt: Besides at night, when must you turn on your headlights?
questions.explanation: You must turn your headlights on whenever you can't clearly see 150 metres ahead. (Driver's Guide p. 81)

choices.text: Whenever you can't clearly see 150 metres ahead

questions.prompt: Why aren't daytime running lights enough for driving at night?
questions.explanation: Daytime running lights aren't bright enough, and your tail lights and instrument panel lights won't be on. (Driver's Guide p. 81)

choices.text: They aren't bright enough, and your tail lights won't be on

questions.prompt: You must switch to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
questions.explanation: Use low beams within 300 metres of oncoming vehicles, and within 150 metres when following another vehicle. (Driver's Guide p. 82)

questions.prompt: The headlights of an oncoming vehicle are blinding you. Where should you look?
questions.explanation: Look slightly down and to the right edge of your lane until the vehicle passes. (Driver's Guide p. 81)

choices.text: Slightly down and to the right edge of your lane

questions.prompt: Your tires lose contact with a wet road and begin to hydroplane. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Don't brake. Release pressure on the accelerator to let the vehicle slow, and steer where you want to go. (Driver's Guide p. 83)

choices.text: Don't brake; ease off the gas and steer where you want to go
Brake firmly until the vehicle stops
Accelerate to push through the water
Turn the wheel sharply to get out of the water

questions.prompt: Which road surface may have black ice?
questions.explanation: If the asphalt looks shiny and black instead of grey-white, it may be black ice. Reduce speed without braking. (Driver's Guide p. 82)

choices.text: Pavement that looks dry and grey-white
Asphalt that looks shiny and black

questions.prompt: Why should you not use cruise control on icy roads?
questions.explanation: If your tires hit ice, cruise control will keep applying the accelerator and you could lose control. (Driver's Guide p. 83)

choices.text: It uses too much fuel in cold weather
It keeps accelerating when the tires hit ice, which can cause a loss of control

questions.prompt: You are stranded in your vehicle in winter, and it is in a safe place. What is usually the safest choice?
questions.explanation: It is usually safer to stay with your vehicle. Run the engine only enough to stay warm, with a window open slightly to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning. (Driver's Guide p. 83)

choices.text: Stay with the vehicle and run the engine sparingly with a window slightly open
Run the engine continuously with the windows closed
Leave the vehicle and wait at the roadside

questions.prompt: When are animals most active near roads?
questions.explanation: Be careful at dusk and dawn, when animals tend to be more active. (Driver's Guide p. 84)

choices.text: In the middle of the day

questions.prompt: After a collision, which of these should you avoid doing?
questions.explanation: Exchange information and record details, but do not discuss who was at fault. (Driver's Guide p. 84)

choices.text: Writing down the names of witnesses

questions.prompt: When passing an emergency vehicle or tow truck stopped with its lights flashing, what is your maximum speed in the lane next to it?
questions.explanation: Slow to 60 km/h, or the posted speed if it is lower, in the lane immediately next to the stopped vehicles. Fines are doubled. (Driver's Guide p. 85)

choices.text: 60 km/h, or the posted speed if lower

questions.prompt: A vehicle with flashing green lights approaches. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Treat a vehicle with flashing green lights like any other emergency vehicle. Volunteer firefighters in some municipalities use them. (Driver's Guide p. 85)

choices.text: Ignore it; green lights mean go
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Treat it like any other emergency vehicle and yield

questions.prompt: A police vehicle has stopped behind you with its lights flashing. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay calm and stay in your vehicle, put it in Park and set the park brake, have your licence, registration, and insurance ready, and wait for instructions. (Driver's Guide p. 86)

choices.text: Get out and walk to the police vehicle
Drive to a well-lit area before stopping
Leave the engine running in Drive
Stay in your vehicle with your documents ready and wait for instructions
